Subject: Question: fee ceiling proration + SKU composition in Exhibit B

Hi Karthik,

Quick question as we're reviewing the most recent exhibit: for the fee "ceiling" in Exhibit B, does the proration mechanism apply at the SKU level or at the consolidated bucket level? Our procurement team is reading the language two ways:

- If a mid-quarter SKU change occurs (we add a premium SKU), do you prorate the fee ceiling for that SKU only, or do you recalibrate the entire bucket's ceiling pro rata?

Also, the SKU composition table references "base units" and "enhanced units" but the mapping in the spreadsheet you sent earlier doesn't explicitly tag which SKUs are eligible for the enhanced band. Can you confirm where to find authoritative SKU classification?

Thanks — would like to resolve before we send Exhibit B back to legal.

Best,
Alex
Senior Procurement Manager
Orion HealthTech

Attachments: SKU_composition_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionht.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: fee ceiling proration + SKU composition in Exhibit B

Alex — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: our standard is to prorate at the bucket level unless parties have explicitly carved out a per-SKU proration in the exhibit. That said, Exhibit B has a legacy clause from the pilot that could be read as SKU-level.

I'll loop in Laura (billing/legal ops) and Jordan (order-schedule owner) to propose a one-liner for the exhibit that removes ambiguity. If Orion prefers per-SKU proration we can accommodate but it will change how we calculate the ceiling for true-ups and may affect the fee smoothing language.

Laura / Jordan — can you weigh in with preferred phrasing and whether we should (a) keep bucket-level proration with an explicit exclusion for mid-period SKU introductions, or (b) allow per-SKU proration and add a cross-reference to the SKU composition annex?

Karthik
Director, GTM Strategy
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionht.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-17T14:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: fee ceiling proration + SKU composition in Exhibit B

Karthik / Alex — quick legal ops take.

We're seeing the ambiguity in two places: the Fee Ceiling paragraph and the SKU Composition table footnote. Recommended path:

1) Replace the Fee Ceiling sentence (Exhibit B, §2.1) with: "Fee ceilings shall be calculated on a consolidated bucket basis and prorated across the entire bucket for any partial-period starts or changes, except where a SKU is expressly designated in the SKU Composition Annex as 'per-SKU proration eligible'."

2) Add an explicit toggle column in the SKU annex labeled "Per-SKU Proration Eligible (Y/N)" and populate it for the SKUs we've agreed will be treated separately. That avoids retroactive recalculation surprises in true-ups.

Pros: preserves our default (bucket-level) economics, gives a clear route to make exceptions. Cons: if Orion wants a lot of SKUs marked Y, it will materially change projected ceilings and could trigger a pricing uplift.

Alex — to speed this, I've attached a short redline of Exhibit B and a draft SKU sheet with the new column. Please review and tell us which SKUs you want marked Y. If legal needs the change in different language, tell us your preferred phrasing and we'll iterate.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Legal Ops Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ExhibitB_v3_redline.pdf (redline stub), SKU_composition_v2.xlsx (updated with column)
From: Alex Wu <alex.wu@orionht.com>

Date: 2026-05-18T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Question: fee ceiling proration + SKU composition in Exhibit B

Laura — this is extremely helpful, thank you.

We reviewed the draft with procurement and legal. Two notes:
1) Procurement prefers bucket-level proration as the default (so your recommendation aligns with our preference).
2) Legal asked that the definition of "per-SKU proration eligible" include a short criteria line: "SKUs that (a) are billed independently for metered usage, or (b) unlock materially different service tiers or capacity profiles." Can we fold that into the annex column description so the parties have objective criteria to mark Y/N?

We'll take the redline and the updated SKU sheet, populate the Y/N column for the three SKUs we intend to treat per-SKU, and return with a single redline from our counsel. Expect that back by EOD Thursday.

Two quick asks for Redwood ops: if we end up with 3 per-SKU markings, can you run a quick sensitivity on the fee ceiling delta (expected % change to bucket ceiling) versus current projections? That will help procurement justify the call.

Thanks — cc'ing Jordan and Marissa for ops/pricing runbook.

— Alex
Senior Procurement Manager, Orion HealthTech
